schemeScope: Combined Ordinary scheme. PDF 12–14 Léamhthuiscint A (with the Paper 2 notes and its mark boxes); 15–17 Léamhthuiscint B; 18–20 Prós Ainmnithe (2A); 21 Prós Roghnach (2B); 22–24 Filíocht Ainmnithe (3A); 25–26 Filíocht Roghnach (3B); 27 modified marking (SMM; 28 is its Paper 1 table). PDF 1–11 belong to Paper 1; 29–32 are blank.
reviewMethod: Every paper page (1–3 cover and instructions, 4–7 the two reading passages, 8–12 literature) and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page; each prompt and scheme slice is asserted against the PDFs by the builder.

nonPoolDecisions: Reading: all ten questions are required; each printed (a)/(b) part is a 5-mark practice card beside the whole question. “3 mharc + 2 mharc” items are order-dependent (first correct point 3, second 2) and stay whole at 0/3/5; single answers allow 0/5.
Reading language: “Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh” is one deduction from each 50-mark passage total; cards state it without applying it inside a part.

Prescribed prose (2A): (a) Dís prints five sub-questions the scheme prices at 5 each: the whole question is a 25-mark card and every sub-question is also a practice card. (b) Oisín i dTír na nÓg is one 25-mark question (five points at 2 + 3).

Prescribed poetry (3A): each poem is a whole 25-mark card with (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9 and one 0–4 Gaeilge deduction; every printed sub-question is also a practice card. 3A(b)(i) An tEarrach Thiar prints three questions, (a) 2, (b) 2 + 2 and (c) 2: the sub-question keeps 0/2/4/6/8 and each question is its own practice card.
Optional prose (2B) and optional poetry (3B) stay whole: the text is open content chosen by the candidate. 3B(b) asks for a modern poem not used in 3B(a).
Choice is not a route: Ceist 2 and Ceist 3 are each A or B; each printed question is one card carrying the printed choice and “Freagair (a) agus (b) anseo.”; no combination cards.
Literature language: “Gaeilge lochtach: 0-4 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh” is one deduction from each 25-mark question, never inside one sub-question.
sourceFindings: Paper 2 = 200: Ceist 1 reading 100 (A An tAthrú Aeráide 50, B Mná agus an Spórt 50; ten questions at (a) 5 + (b) 5 each), Ceist 2 prose 50 (A Prós Ainmnithe: (a) Dís 25 + (b) Oisín i dTír na nÓg 25; or B Prós Roghnach: (a) gearrscéal 25 + (b) scéal béaloidis 25), Ceist 3 poetry 50 (A Filíocht Ainmnithe: (a) Géibheann 25 + (b) An tEarrach Thiar 25; or B Filíocht Roghnach: (a) 25 + (b) 25).

The scheme’s text layer stores nine boxed headings with the page body (“CEIST 1 (A + B) - LÉAMHTHUISCINT - 100 marc”, “A – (50 marc)”, “B – (50 marc)”, the CEIST 2/3 and section boxes); the builder removes those exact strings (count pinned).

Each reading passage ends with the scheme’s penalty and mark-box instructions (“Nóta: Gearrfar pionós i ngeall ar iomarcaíocht. Léireofar an pionós …”, “Eolas (50 marc) = … E (50) = G (0-5) = - Iom =”); the last part’s answer key ends before them.

Each literature answer ends with “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0-4 …]” and, for poetry, the mark-panel line “Léirigh mionbhriseadh na marcanna: E (25) = 25 G (0-4) = -”; both are kept out of the answer keys and the deduction is its own criterion.
Reading B Ceist 1(b) prints one answer without a price (“D’éirigh leo áit a bhaint amach …”); the question’s own (5 mharc) is its price.
No 2020 card existed before this review; the 52 cards are new.
